source.title: Steering Without Breaking: Mechanistically Informed Interventions for Discrete Diffusion Language Models
source.authors: Han-Han Zhou; Shamik Roy; Rashmi Gangadharaiah

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies SAE feature emergence and cross-model feature alignment, but does not test whether increasing dictionary size on the same activations splits coarse features into finer ones.
record.gate_note: The paper trains SAEs of different sizes on different models and measures cross-model feature alignment. It does not perform a matched-activation SAE dictionary-size sweep or measure whether child features partition a parent feature's inputs. Cross-model alignment results are recorded under fits_no_version; SAE configurations and steering results do not test the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper trains TopK SAEs on four diffusion LMs as a tool for steering. It never varies dictionary size on fixed activations and never measures splitting, absorption, latent decomposition or feature families. It cites Towards Monosemanticity only as a general SAE reference and does not use or discuss splitting. So 'cites_only' (T6) fits better than 'discusses'.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is correct as far as it goes. The paper's main conclusion, however, concerns temporal commitment of attributes during denoising and adaptive steering schedules. The alignment result is a side finding that the training objective shapes feature geometry. Nothing is concluded about splitting.
record.recipe_differences: No attempt to reproduce or test the feature-splitting method.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-model SAE alignment: MDLM–SEDD mean best-match about 0.08 (near random); MDLM–Dream 0.23 mean, 0.54 max; MDLM–LLaDA 0.15 mean, 0.47 max. Dream→MDLM matches exceed MDLM→Dream, which the authors read as Dream's SAE learning more specific features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature directions align more across diffusion LMs sharing a loss family than across models sharing architecture but differing in loss.

record.problems: The study does not test feature splitting. Its cross-model comparisons change model, architecture, training objective, activation space, and SAE configuration together, so they cannot isolate dictionary size.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version rows were available. Steering outcomes, SAE training configurations, and other interpretability results do not measure size-dependent feature splitting.

untested.parts: No sweep of SAE dictionary size on the same activations; no coarse-to-fine latent mapping.
Large models are used, but there is no splitting measurement and no open SAE releases.
No nested feature families or concept hierarchy.
No parent/child firing or absorption analysis; no size or sparsity variation.
No decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents; no novel-latent analysis.
No comparison of training objectives (e.g., Matryoshka) and no splitting measure.

record.verdict_notes: Off-topic for feature splitting. The 'directional asymmetry' remark loosely echoes the idea that wider SAEs give finer features. It compares different models with different d_model, though, so it cannot count as evidence for V1 or V5.

versions.untested_parts: No dictionary-size sweep on the same activations; no parent-to-child feature or input-partition measurement.
Uses large DLMs, but does not test size-dependent splitting or open SAE releases.
No nested feature-family or concept-hierarchy test.
No parent-child firing, absorption, or size/sparsity comparison.
No decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents or assessment of novel latents.
No objective-induced splitting test or comparison with Matryoshka SAEs.

rows.subject: MDLM-124M ↔ SEDD-124M
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE feature directions across models with the same GPT-2 architecture and different diffusion objectives.
rows.measure: Cross-model best-match cosine similarity and maximum pairwise similarity
rows.value: Mean best-match cosine 0.08–0.085 across attributes; maximum pairwise similarity 0.125.
rows.locator: §3, Figure 3d; Appendix D.5, Table 36 and Key observations
rows.note: The paper describes the features as near-orthogonal across these models. This compares independently trained model SAEs, not dictionary sizes on shared activations.
rows.check: Cross-model decoder alignment between MDLM and SEDD (different loss), not a dictionary-size comparison. The link to no version is correct.

rows.subject: MDLM-124M ↔ Dream-7B
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE feature directions after projection into shared vocabulary space.
rows.measure: Mean best-match cosine similarity and maximum individual feature-pair cosine
rows.value: Mean best-match similarity 0.23; individual feature pairs reach 0.54 cosine.
rows.locator: §3, Figure 3d; Appendix D.5, Table 36 and Key observations
rows.note: The authors interpret the directional asymmetry as Dream features mapping more cleanly to MDLM counterparts while MDLM features are more diffuse. This is not a matched SAE-size comparison.
rows.check: Vocabulary-projected alignment between MDLM and Dream. The authors' reading that Dream's SAE has 'more specific features' confounds model, width, d_model and architecture, so it cannot bear on V1 or V5.

rows.subject: MDLM-124M ↔ LLaDA-8B
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE feature directions after projection into shared vocabulary space.
rows.measure: Mean best-match cosine similarity and maximum individual feature-pair cosine
rows.value: Mean best-match similarity 0.15; individual feature pairs reach 0.47 cosine.
rows.locator: §3, Figure 3d; Appendix D.5, Table 36 and Key observations
rows.note: The paper reports cross-model feature alignment, not splitting within an SAE as dictionary size grows.
rows.check: Vocabulary-projected alignment between MDLM and LLaDA; same issue as r2. Not a splitting measure.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
